newsitem.title: FRANCE: French Left divided over Europe single currency.
newsitem.headline: French Left divided over Europe single currency.

text.p: Leaders of the French Left struggled to find common ground on Europe on Saturday amid glaring policy differences over European Union plans for a single currency.

"Let's not let the French Left be held hostage by the single currency," Communist Party leader Robert Hue told a seminar also attended by Socialist Party leader Lionel Jospin and the Greens' Dominique Voynet.
The opposition parties, hoping to topple the ruling centre-right government in 1998 elections, said they aimed to cooperate on building social policies in Europe.
But they remained starkly at odds over EU plans for economic integration.
Hue, for instance, criticised Jospin for backing EU plans for the single currency from 1999 and said that the Maastricht Treaty's free-market prescriptions were a recipe for recession in France.
Jospin in turn rejected Hue's call for a referendum on the single currency.

He said French people had already had a vote in a cliffhanger 1992 vote that approved the Maastricht treaty and that only conservative President Jacques Chirac, a backer of the single currency, had the power to call a referendum in France.
Voynet said the Greens had never ruled out a single currency but accused EU governments of failing to take account of social and ecological issues in European integration. REUTER
